subject: AcmeBank — follow-up: region pinning & cross-region failover
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Wallace <ethan.wallace@acmebank.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 15:22:00 +0000
Subject: AcmeBank — follow-up: region pinning & cross-region failover

Hi Ethan / Laura —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and a couple of follow-ups we promised:

Summary of call:
- Primary ask: ensure customer data for EU customers stays within EU regions and have an explicit region-pinning + failover plan.
- Questions raised: backups/replication, encryption key residency, audit logs retention, and how automatic cross-region failover behaves.

What I attached: 1) redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (SOC2 summary + controls) and 2) region-pinning-diagram.png (high-level failover flows).

Quick answers / clarifications (high level):
- Region pinning: we support explicit per-tenant region pinning (you can pin to us-east, eu-west, or ap-south regions).
- Failover: automatic failover is opt-in; by default we won't cross-route traffic. Failover can be configured to: manual only, automated on regional outage, or active-active where traffic is mirrored.
- Backups: point-in-time backups are replicated to a customer-designated secondary region for DR.
- Keys: we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations; you can choose residency for key material where supported by the cloud provider.
- Logs & retention: audit/event logs default to 90 days; longer retention is available as an add-on.

Action items / next steps:
1) Could you confirm whether Acme requires: a) strict in-region processing for EU customers (no cross-region processing under any failure mode), or b) in-region by default but allowed failover to US/APAC under emergency DR?
2) If strict in-region is required, we should schedule a short technical call to go over architecture options (Private deployment vs Dedicated + VPC controls).
3) I'll loop in our Solutions Engineer (Marissa) and Product (Vanessa) to capture any requirements for the security questionnaire.

Proposed times for a technical deep dive next week: Wed 08/18 10:00–11:00 PDT or Thu 08/19 14:00–15:00 PDT. Please let me know what works.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

From: Ethan Wallace <ethan.wallace@acmebank.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmebank.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: AcmeBank — follow-up: region pinning & cross-region failover

Thanks Aditya — very helpful recap and the attachments look useful. A couple of clarifying questions from our side before the deep dive:

1) Cross-region failover behavior: if we opt for "in-region by default with emergency failover", what specifically triggers the automated failover? Is it based on provider-region health metrics only, or do you also support application-level health checks and out-of-band triggers from our side? We need to make sure failover won't move EU customer data to the US without an explicit policy approval.

2) Backups & replication: are backups encrypted with the same customer-managed key? Is the secondary DR copy guaranteed to remain in the pinned region (i.e., EU) if strict in-region is selected?

3) Key residency: for KMS/HSM integrations that store keys in EU, will any of the key material ever transit or be accessed from US-based control plane components? We have legal constraints around key access.

4) Audit logs: can you provide a sample schema for the audit logs and confirm whether event logs (e.g., inference request metadata) can be restricted to EU storage?

If you can outline those items in advance of the deep dive that would be great. We are leaning toward strict in-region for regulated products but want to understand the trade-offs.

—Ethan
Ethan Wallace
Senior Product Manager, Data Platform | Acme Bank
ethan.wallace@acmebank.com | +1 (617) 555-0199
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 18:30:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: AcmeBank — follow-up: region pinning & cross-region failover

Internal note —

Ethan's questions are the ones we usually see for regulated banks. Proposed responses for the deep dive (we can polish before sending to them):
- Failover triggers: support provider-region health + app-level probes + manual triggers from Acme (we should offer a policy option that prevents automatic cross-region for EU-pinned tenants).
- Backups: can be configured to remain in-region for strict in-region customers; by default DR copies are kept in a secondary region but we can change this per-contract.
- Keys: with customer-managed KMS keys (BYOK) the key material remains in the provider EU KMS; control plane operations require RBAC but we can provide an architecture diagram showing no key material leaves EU.
- Logs: we can route audit/event logs to an EU-only bucket and redact any global routing metadata if required.

Ask: Aditya — if Acme wants strict in-region for production, recommend Private deployment (VPC + Dedicated) so we can commit contractually to data residency and offer longer retention SLAs. Vanessa, please confirm any commercial/technical constraints for offering in-region-only backups and extended log retention (pricing impact).

We'll draft a short response to Ethan that lays out those options and confirms the deep-dive times.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Wallace <ethan.wallace@acmebank.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 11:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: AcmeBank — follow-up: region pinning & cross-region failover

Ethan — thanks for the questions. Below are concrete answers; happy to expand in the deep dive.

1) Cross-region failover triggers
- Options we offer: manual-only, automated-on-region-outage (provider health signals + service-level monitors), and automated-with-app-probes (hooks you can provide).
- For strict in-region customers we can set policy to manual-only: we will not automatically route EU-pinned traffic to any non-EU region under any failure condition without explicit authorization.

2) Backups & replication
- Backups are encrypted at-rest using either Redwood-managed keys or your customer-managed KMS (BYOK). If you select BYOK and choose EU KMS, snapshot encryption keys remain in that EU KMS.
- For strict in-region: DR copies remain in EU and are not replicated to US/APAC. For non-strict setups we replicate to a secondary region (configured per contract).

3) Key residency & control plane access
- With BYOK your key material resides in the provider KMS (e.g., AWS KMS eu-west-1). Redwood's control plane uses role-based access and never exports raw key material. We can provide an architecture diagram and an options matrix for HSM-backed keys if you require FIPS/HSM-level assurance.

4) Audit logs & event data
- Schema: timestamp, tenant_id, request_id, operation, resource, requester_identity, src_ip, user_agent, response_status, ingest_region.
- We can route audit and request metadata to an EU-only storage bucket and redact or exclude ingest_region if you prefer. Default retention is 90 days; we can contract for multi-year retention at an additional storage/ingest fee.

Attachments: re-attached the SOC2 summary and the region-pinning diagram.

Next steps:
- If you confirm "strict in-region" for regulated workloads, we'll prepare a Private deployment proposal and SOW with explicit residency guarantees.
- Proposed deep-dive: Thu 08/19 14:00–15:00 PDT (works for our SE/Product). Please confirm and I will send calendar invite.

Thanks and speak soon —
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
